subject: radiology
title: Radiation toxicity and tissue tolerance

steps.tx: Tissue response to radiation depends on **radiosensitivity**, which is highest in rapidly dividing cells. The most sensitive tissues include lymphoid tissue, bone marrow, the intestinal epithelium and gonads. Bone, cartilage, muscle, nerve and the CNS are comparatively radioresistant. Cartilage is the classic most radioresistant tissue in exam questions. Embryonic tissue is the most sensitive of all.

rows: Lymphoid, bone marrow, gut epithelium, gonads

steps.tx: Tolerance doses are quoted as TD 5/5 style values for organs. The whole **liver** tolerates about 40 Gy, while two-thirds of the volume tolerates about 45 Gy. Rectum tolerates about 60 Gy, bladder about 65 Gy and vagina about 90 Gy. The **ovary** is the most radiosensitive pelvic organ, with tolerance around 2 to 3 Gy.

steps.tx: Skin reaction starts with **erythema** within about two weeks of fractionated therapy, followed by dry or moist desquamation. Mucositis also begins around two weeks and heals about two months after therapy. Chronic skin changes such as atrophy and hyperpigmentation appear months later. Radiation pneumonitis, proctitis and myelitis are the main late organ-specific toxicities.

steps.tx: Long-term risks include **radiation-induced malignancy**, such as papillary thyroid carcinoma after childhood exposure, and radon-linked lung cancer. Radiation carries an increased risk for thyroid and salivary tumours. Protection uses amifostine, a radioprotector that reduces xerostomia after head and neck radiotherapy, and PET helps separate necrosis from recurrence.
